main_text.l: Nec mora iussus adest, primóque à limine regem
Compellat Sates, Salue rex, (inquit) & audi.
Quid sceleris media patratum euenerit Vrbe.
Ecce, fuit pecoris quidam ditissimus Gnus,
Et pecoris quiddam contrà pauperrimus Gnus:
Illi mille greges, quis huic tantùm Gnica, Verùm
Chara fuit, primis paruà quam eduxerat annis,
Ipso etiam gremio, & lecto dignatus eodem.
Ille aduentantem casu excepturus amicum,
(Proh facinus) bubúsque suis ouibusq; pepercit:
At miseram arripiens Vicini pauperis, eheu,
O rex, mactauit sauus coxitq; bidente (quit)
Dauid ad hac animo graujter comotus, At (in-
Sic saueat dextrum mihi numen, Vt iste cruentas
Dignus q.ui proprio pendat Vel sanguine poenas,
Pauperis octuplici pensabit fœnore damnum.
Hac ille, intuitus sauo quem lumine Sates.
Ergo( ait )infelix, audi, quid numinis ira
Nuntiet, ô regum rex indignissime, tenè
Tam subitò oblitum quanto te euexit honore
Cunctipotens, inopem, mediisque ab ouilibus olim
Acceptum, & sauì toties totisque leonis
Faucibus ereptum, solij quum sede locaret,
Sacrarétque isto tantum diadémate regem?
Ten miserum tali pollutum cade, quietem
Ducere, quem ad pœnam poscant pro immanibus
aufis
Crimina? sic igitur turpem traducere Vitam
Amplexus medios inter?geminóne nocentem

Several words are doubtful in the scan: "Gnus" and "Gnica" and "Sates" appear to be printed initial-letter forms (Greek-like or woodcut initials), transcribed as printed; "Sates" for Nathan's speech is likely a printed initial. Line-end hyphen in "(in-" and "(quit)" are as printed. Marks such as "Vt iste" and "Pauperis" are as read.
